# Inclusions between complexity classes

[Chapter index](index.md) · [Major endpoints](endpoints-and-hierarchies.md) · [Verifier models](verifiers-counting-interaction.md)

<!-- Generated by scripts/class_inclusions.py; edit the script, not this page. -->

Each cell says whether the row class is contained in the column class: what the library proves, and otherwise what is known.

| Mark | Meaning |
|---|---|
| ✓ | A library theorem states the inclusion; the mark links to it |
| = | The library proves both inclusions |
| ✓* | The inclusion follows by chaining library theorems |
| ✗ | The library proves that the inclusion fails |
| (✓) | Known to hold, not yet formalized here |
| (✗) | Known to fail, not yet formalized here |
| ? | An open question in the literature |

Known non-inclusions all come from hierarchy theorems or lower bounds: `Z ⊄ Y` gives `A ⊄ B` whenever `Z ⊆ A` and `B ⊆ Y`. For the uniform classes, complements are used too: `NP ⊆ coNP` holds exactly when `coNP ⊆ NP`.

The uniform grid compares classes of bit-string languages, that is, the classes at the encoding `encBits`. Most of the linked inclusion theorems are more general and hold for every injective encoding `enc`. The strict inclusions behind the ✗ marks (`L ⊊ PSPACE`, `P ⊊ EXP`, `NP ⊊ NEXP`) are stated only for `encBits`, and they can fail for other encodings: with a single instance, every class is the same. The circuit classes are nonuniform, so they are not compared with the uniform classes: nonuniform AC⁰ already contains undecidable unary languages.

## Literature layer

These unconditional results, closed under chaining and complements, decide every cell that is not marked ?. A cell marked ? is open: neither the inclusion nor its failure follows from them.

| Fact | Source |
|---|---|
| L ⊆ NL | by definition |
| NL ⊆ P | reachability in polynomial time, Arora–Barak Chapter 4 |
| P ⊆ ZPP | by definition |
| ZPP ⊆ RP | Gill 1977 (`Gill1977`) |
| RP ⊆ NP | Gill 1977 |
| RP ⊆ BPP | Gill 1977 |
| NP ⊆ MA | by definition |
| BPP ⊆ MA | by definition |
| MA ⊆ AM | Babai 1985 (`Babai1985`) |
| AM ⊆ PH | AM ⊆ Π₂ᵖ, Babai 1985 |
| NP ⊆ PH | by definition |
| BPP ⊆ BQP | Bernstein–Vazirani 1997 (`BernsteinVazirani1997`) |
| MA ⊆ QMA | by definition |
| BQP ⊆ QMA | by definition |
| QMA ⊆ PP | Kitaev–Watrous 2000 (`KitaevWatrous2000`) |
| NP ⊆ PP | Gill 1977 |
| PP ⊆ P^#P | by definition |
| PH ⊆ P^#P | Toda 1991 (`Toda1991`) |
| P^#P ⊆ PSPACE | counting by enumeration, Arora–Barak Chapter 17 |
| PSPACE ⊆ IP | Shamir 1992 (`Shamir1992`) |
| IP ⊆ PSPACE | evaluating the game tree in polynomial space, Arora–Barak Chapter 8 |
| PSPACE ⊆ EXP | counting configurations, Arora–Barak Chapter 4 |
| EXP ⊆ NEXP | by definition |
| PSPACE ⊄ NL | NL ⊆ SPACE(log² n) (Savitch 1970, `Savitch1970`) ⊊ PSPACE by the space hierarchy theorem (Stearns–Hartmanis–Lewis 1965, `StearnsHartmanisLewis1965`) |
| EXP ⊄ P | time hierarchy theorem, Arora–Barak Chapter 3 |
| NEXP ⊄ NP | nondeterministic time hierarchy theorem (Žák 1983, `Zak1983`) |
| NEXP ⊄ coNP | NEXP ⊆ coNP would give NP ⊆ coNP, so NP = coNP ⊇ NEXP, contradicting NP ⊊ NEXP |
| AC⁰ ⊆ ACC⁰ | by definition |
| ACC⁰ ⊆ TC⁰ | a MOD gate is a sum of threshold gates |
| TC⁰ ⊆ NC¹ | iterated addition in logarithmic depth |
| NC¹ ⊆ AC¹ | by definition |
| AC¹ ⊆ NC² | balanced fan-in-two trees |
| NC² ⊆ P/poly | by definition |
| ACC⁰ ⊄ AC⁰ | parity is not in AC⁰ (Furst–Saxe–Sipser 1984, `FurstSaxeSipser1984`; Ajtai 1983, `Ajtai1983`) |

## Regenerating

Run `python3 scripts/class_inclusions.py` after adding an inclusion theorem, and `python3 scripts/class_inclusions.py --check` to test whether this page is current. New theorems named `A_subset_B`, `A_ssubset_B`, `A_eq_B` or `A_not_subset_B` between classes of a grid appear automatically. The script refuses to write a page on which the library proves something the literature layer calls open or false.
